The Otter bot joined two confidential meetings on my behalf and recorded the whole thing, then emailed every member an absurd, inaccurate "outline" after.

I just deleted my account because of that, also they share conversations with everyone in the meeting by DEFAULT, it wasn't nice receiving a message from a co-worker telling me that he received an email with the transcription it generated.

I stopped using them when I saw they share with everyone by default. I wanted the notes only for myself so I could be more present in meetings but not at the expense of making everyone feel like they have to watch what they're saying because it's being transcribed.
I have opened a support ticket with screenshots but there is no response, and according to Twitter they are essentially not reviewing tickets from free users at the moment.

An AI researcher said Otter recorded a Zoom meeting with investors, then shared a transcription including 'intimate, confidential details' about a business discussed after he had left the meeting — those portions of the conversation ended up killing a deal.

A lawyer invited OtterAI to a confidential meeting; the commenter read Otter's privacy statement and found they retain data in the cloud and use 'anonymized' recordings as future training data, and refused to continue with the bot present.

A lawyer used Otter to record and transcribe a confidential meeting about a child custody case; participants' first awareness of the recording was a summary email at the end. When asked, the company dismissed responsibility, saying it was up to subscribers to use the product appropriately.

I remember being on sensitive zoom calls and seeing Otter.ai join. Had to track down which person was using it, and even they were clueless as to how it got there, and the client kept rejoining despite the user trying to stop it.

I use Otter pretty religiously to record all work meetings that I participate in... it doesn't do an amazing job with English in various accents — I've noticed Google Recorder on Android is better in this regard — but it's good enough. Nice product.

Otter sent a survey referencing the title of a sensitive recording, which spooked the journalist into thinking his recordings had been shared with China; Otter later reassured him this was not the case.

Most of the companies in this space (Fireflies, Otter, Vowel, ~Chorus, ~Gong) use external APIs for speech-to-text, meaning unencrypted audio and plain text traverses a 3rd party server — a security risk if breached.

I'm generally a 'hater' of the cloud, and I have to admit that Otter is very good. I used it speaking with someone using airpods on a shitty internet connection, with no noticeable drop in accuracy. Even spelled uncommon last names correctly.
Otter is the only thing approaching affordable for individuals, but I don't really trust it given they're playing fast and loose with user data.
